label: The doorkeepers, treasurers, army captains, and officers of state
atlas_section: 1 Chronicles pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): 1 Chronicles 26-27, the courses of the doorkeepers and their own charge over the treasuries, the officers and judges for the outward business of Israel, the twelve captains of the army by monthly course, the chiefs of the twelve tribes, the overseers of the king's own possessions, and the closing officers of state, including 'Ahithophel was the king's counsellor.'

label: For three transgressions of Edom, and for four
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 1:11-12, judgment on Edom for pursuing his brother (Israel) with the sword without pity.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 1:13-15, judgment on Ammon for ripping up the women with child of Gilead to enlarge its own border.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: For three transgressions of Israel, and for four
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 2:6-16, the book's own longest and central indictment -- Israel selling the righteous for silver and the poor for a pair of shoes, recalling the Lord's own deliverance from Egypt and the raising up of prophets and Nazarites, closing on the day none shall escape.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: You only have I known of all the families of the earth: the Lord's necessity to prophesy
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 3, 'you only have I known of all the families of the earth: therefore I will punish you for all your iniquities' -- the lion has roared, who will not fear? -- closing on the altars of Beth-el visited and the winter and summer houses smitten.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: The kine of Bashan; five judgments sent, and Israel still did not return
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 4, the women of Samaria rebuked as 'kine of Bashan,' the five-fold refrain 'yet have ye not returned unto me, saith the Lord' over famine, drought, blight, pestilence, and overthrow, closing on 'prepare to meet thy God, O Israel.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: A lamentation for Israel; seek the Lord, and ye shall live
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 5:1-17, 'the virgin of Israel is fallen' -- a lamentation taken up against the house of Israel -- and the call to seek the Lord rather than Beth-el or Gilgal, with 'let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream' at its own center.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord; I hate, I despise your feast days
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 5:18-27, 'woe unto you that desire the day of the Lord... it is darkness, and not light' -- the Lord's own rejection of empty feasts and offerings without justice, closing on captivity 'beyond Damascus.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Woe to them that are at ease in Zion, and trust in the mountain of Samaria
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 6, woe to the complacent who lie upon beds of ivory and are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph -- a nation raised up against Israel from the entering in of Hamath unto the river of the wilderness.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: The first vision: the locusts
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 7:1-3, the Lord shews Amos a plague of locusts devouring the land; Amos intercedes, 'by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small,' and the Lord repents of it.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. First of five visions (7:1-3, 7:4-6, 7:7-9, 8:1-3, 9:1-10), the master brief's own named 'per vision' granularity.

label: The second vision: the devouring fire
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 7:4-6, the Lord shews Amos a fire that devours the great deep; Amos again intercedes, and the Lord again repents.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Second of five visions.

label: The third vision: the plumbline
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 7:7-9, the Lord standing upon a wall made by a plumbline -- 'I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more' -- the high places of Isaac laid waste, and judgment on the house of Jeroboam.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Third of five visions -- this is the first vision the text itself no longer records the Lord repenting of.

label: The fourth vision: the basket of summer fruit
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 8:1-3, a basket of summer fruit -- 'the end is come upon my people of Israel' -- a wordplay between the Hebrew for 'summer fruit' and 'end,' a literary-structure fact, not textual criticism.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Fourth of five visions.

label: A famine of hearing the words of the Lord
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 8:4-14, indictment of merchants who swallow up the needy and falsify the balances, and the Lord's own promise of 'a famine... of hearing the words of the Lord' -- they shall run to and fro to seek it, and shall not find it.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: The fifth vision: the Lord standing by the altar; none shall escape
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 9:1-10, the Lord standing upon the altar commanding the lintel smitten -- though they dig into hell or climb to heaven, none shall escape -- yet 'I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob,' as Israel is sifted among the nations like corn in a sieve.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Fifth of five visions.

label: The tabernacle of David raised up again
atlas_section: Amos pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Amos 9:11-15, the book's own closing restoration oracle -- 'in that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David that is fallen' -- planting Israel again upon their own land, never again to be pulled up.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Translation/literary fact, not textual criticism: this is the passage James cites at the Jerusalem council (Acts 15:16-17).

label: The vision of the four beasts
atlas_section: Daniel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Daniel 7, dated 'the first year of Belshazzar king of Babylon' -- four great beasts rising from the sea, the Ancient of days seated in judgment, and 'one like the Son of man' given an everlasting dominion; the fourth beast's own interpretation given to Daniel by one who stood by.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind: no comparably reusable anchor exists in this app's own compiled data for Belshazzar's own first regnal year specifically (unlike chapters 9/10-12, below), per this file's own header note. First of Daniel's own remaining visions, the master brief's own named 'per vision' granularity.

label: The vision of the ram and the goat
atlas_section: Daniel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Daniel 8, dated 'the third year of the reign of king Belshazzar' -- a ram with two horns overthrown by a fierce one-horned goat, whose own great horn is broken and replaced by four; Gabriel's own interpretation of the vision, which Daniel could not understand and which made him sick.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note (same reasoning as dan_vision_of_the_four_beasts).

atlas_section: Ecclesiastes pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ecclesiastes 3, the poem 'to every thing there is a season' (3:1-8), followed by the Preacher's own reflection on God's own work in its time, and the like end of man and beast.

atlas_section: Ecclesiastes pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ecclesiastes 4, the Preacher's own observation of oppression under the sun, the vanity of toil pursued in envy or alone, the value of two better than one, and the vanity of popularity, closing 'this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: A warning to keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God
atlas_section: Ecclesiastes pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ecclesiastes 5:1-7, a warning to approach God's own house with care, to be slow to vow, and to fear God rather than multiply words.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: The vanity of riches, and the ignorance of man's own future
atlas_section: Ecclesiastes pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ecclesiastes 5:8-6:12, the Preacher's own reflection on oppression and the love of money never satisfied, the emptiness of riches without the power to enjoy them, and the shortness of man's life, closing on man's own ignorance of what is good for him or what shall come after him.

ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 13, judgment on prophets who prophesy out of their own hearts, 'daubing' a flimsy wall 'with untempered morter,' and on women who sew pillows to all armholes, hunting souls with false comfort.

label: These men have set up their idols in their heart: though Noah, Daniel, and Job were in it
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 14, elders who come to inquire of the Lord while holding idols in their own heart answered directly, and a fourfold judgment (sword, famine, beasts, pestilence) so severe that even Noah, Daniel, and Job -- named together as three righteous men -- would deliver only their own souls, not their sons or daughters.

label: What is the vine tree more than any tree? It is cast into the fire for fuel
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 15, a short parable -- the wood of the vine, useless even before the fire has scorched it, useless still after -- so shall Jerusalem's own inhabitants be given to the fire.

label: Jerusalem pictured as an unfaithful wife, from birth to harlotry to the everlasting covenant restored
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 16, this book's own longest single chapter -- Jerusalem's own birth unwashed and unswaddled, betrothed and adorned by the Lord, then playing the harlot with every passer-by, more corrupt than Sodom and Samaria (her own 'sisters,' 16:46-49, whose own sin is named as pride, fulness of bread, and idleness, neglecting the poor and needy), closing on the Lord's own remembrance of his covenant and an everlasting covenant yet to come.

label: Two great eagles and a vine: the parable of the transplanted cedar sprig
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 17, a riddle of two great eagles and a vine, interpreted as Babylon's own transplanting of Judah's own king and the folly of turning to Egypt instead, closing on the Lord's own promise to plant a tender sprig of the cedar's own highest branch upon a high mountain.

label: The soul that sinneth, it shall die: the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 18, a sustained argument against the proverb 'the fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge' -- each soul answers for its own righteousness or wickedness, a wicked man's own repentance genuinely saves him, and a righteous man's own turning to sin genuinely condemns him -- closing on 'I have no pleasure in the death of him that dieth... wherefore turn yourselves, and live ye.'

label: Take up a lamentation for the princes of Israel: a lioness, her whelps, and a wasted vine
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 19, a lamentation in the form of two allegories -- a lioness whose whelps are both taken captive, and a fruitful vine plucked up in fury, planted in the wilderness, and set on fire.

label: The bloody city: a catalogue of Jerusalem's own sins, and the dross in the furnace
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 22, a long catalogue of Jerusalem's own sins -- shedding blood, dishonoring parents, oppressing strangers, defiling the sabbath -- pictured as dross in a furnace, and a search for 'a man... that should make up the hedge, and stand in the gap before me for the land, that I should not destroy it,' but none is found.

label: Aholah and Aholibah: two sisters, Samaria and Jerusalem, both unfaithful
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 23, an extended allegory of two sisters -- Aholah (Samaria) and Aholibah (Jerusalem) -- both playing the harlot with Egypt and Assyria and Babylon in turn, judged by the very lovers they once courted.

label: Oracles against Ammon, Moab, Edom, and Philistia
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 25, four short oracles against the nations immediately bordering Judah -- Ammon rebuked for rejoicing over the sanctuary's own profaning, Moab for saying 'the house of Judah is like unto all the heathen,' Edom for taking vengeance, and Philistia for old, perpetual hatred.

label: The day of the Lord is near, a cloudy day: it shall be the time of the heathen
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 30:1-19, no new date given -- a further oracle of the day of the Lord upon Egypt and her own helpers, Ethiopia, Libya, and Lydia, her own cities named one by one for judgment.

label: If the watchman see the sword come, and blow not the trumpet: the watchman charge renewed
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 33:1-20, no new date given -- the watchman's own responsibility restated in general terms (a wicked man turning from his sin shall live; a righteous man turning to sin shall die in it), preparing for the specific, dated news that follows.

label: Woe be to the shepherds of Israel: I myself will search my sheep, and seek them out
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 34, Israel's own shepherds rebuked for feeding themselves rather than the flock, the Lord's own promise to search for his own sheep himself, and 'my servant David' set up as one shepherd and prince over a covenant of peace.

label: Set thy face against mount Seir, and prophesy against it: Edom's own perpetual hatred judged
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 35, judgment against Mount Seir (Edom) for perpetual hatred and violence against Israel in the day of her calamity.

label: Ye mountains of Israel, hear the word of the Lord: a new heart also will I give you
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 36, the mountains of Israel promised fruitfulness and a returning people, the Lord's own act 'not for your sakes... but for mine holy name's sake,' and the promise of a new heart and a new spirit -- 'I will take away the stony heart out of your flesh, and I will give you an heart of flesh' (36:26).

label: Son of man, can these bones live? The valley of dry bones, and the two sticks joined
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 37, the vision of a valley full of very dry bones, joined together, covered with flesh, and given breath -- 'these bones are the whole house of Israel' -- and a sign-act of two sticks, for Judah and for Joseph/Ephraim, joined into one in the prophet's own hand as a picture of a reunited kingdom under one shepherd forever.

label: Set thy face against Gog, the land of Magog: the Lord's own judgment on the final invader
atlas_section: Ezekiel pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezekiel 38-39, an extensive oracle against Gog of the land of Magog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal, gathering a great confederacy against a peaceful, regathered Israel -- overthrown by the Lord's own hand, an earthquake, and confusion, buried in 'the valley of Hamon-gog,' closing on the promise that the Lord will no more hide his own face from the house of Israel, having poured out his Spirit upon them.

label: The line of Cain, and Lamech's song
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 4:17-24, Cain's descendants through Lamech, closing with Lamech's own song of vengeance.
ref_note: General-kind: a genealogical list spanning many generations, no single dateable moment or place of its own.

label: The generations of Adam to Noah
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 5, the toledoth of Adam through Noah's own sons -- one container for the whole genealogical chapter, per this batch's own granularity guidance ('genealogies = their own units'), rather than a separate heading for each of the 26 already-compiled Theographic birth/lifetime/death micro-events this range also touches (theo-4 through theo-37) -- those stay legally reachable via the verse's own EVENT membership popover; this container is the chapter's own reader heading.
ref_note: General-kind: spans ~1,500 years of genealogy, no single dateable moment or place.

label: Noah's three sons, and the Table of Nations
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 9:18-19 (Noah's three sons, of whom the whole earth was overspread) through Genesis 10 (the Table of Nations proper) -- one container for the whole list, same 'genealogies = their own units' reasoning as gen_generations_adam_to_noah; overlaps theo-87's own narrower 'Nimrod's kingdom begins' (10:8-12) legally.
ref_note: General-kind: a genealogical/national list, no single dateable moment or place of its own.

label: The generations of Shem to Terah
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 11:10-32, the toledoth of Shem through Terah (Abram's own father) -- one container for the whole genealogical chapter, closing with Terah's family in Ur, same reasoning as gen_generations_adam_to_noah; overlaps the existing theo-34..theo-70 birth/lifetime/death micro-events and ab_ur's own narrative leg legally (those stay reachable via EVENT membership; this container is the chapter's own reader heading).
ref_note: General-kind: spans centuries of genealogy, no single dateable moment or place of its own.

label: The children of Nahor
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 22:20-24, a brief genealogical notice of Nahor's own children (including Rebekah's own father Bethuel).
ref_note: General-kind: a brief genealogical notice, no place or date of its own stated.

label: Abraham's later years; the sons of Keturah
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 25:1-6, Abraham's marriage to Keturah, and gifts to his sons by his concubines.
ref_note: General-kind: spans an unstated number of Abraham's own remaining years, no single dateable moment or place of its own.

label: The generations of Esau
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 36, Esau's own descendants and the kings of Edom -- one container for the whole genealogical/king-list chapter, same 'genealogies = their own units' reasoning as this file's other list containers.
ref_note: General-kind: a genealogical and king list spanning generations, no single dateable moment or place of its own.

label: The genealogy of the seventy who came into Egypt
atlas_section: Genesis pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Genesis 46:6-27, the full genealogical list of Jacob's own household who came into Egypt, closing 'all the souls... were threescore and ten' -- one container for the whole list, same 'genealogies = their own units' reasoning.
ref_note: General-kind: a genealogical list, no single dateable moment or place of its own beyond the surrounding je_beersheba/je_goshen narrative legs' own dating.

label: The burden which Habakkuk the prophet did see.
kjv_superscription: HAB.1.1, the book's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: GENERAL-kind: oracle, no date of its own claimed, per this file's own header note. Content: Habakkuk's own first complaint -- violence and iniquity unanswered -- and the Lord's own answer, raising up the Chaldeans as his instrument of judgment.

label: Habakkuk's second complaint, and the Lord's answer: the just shall live by his faith
atlas_section: Habakkuk pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Habakkuk 1:12-2:20, the prophet's own second complaint (how can a just God use so wicked an instrument?), his own watching upon the tower for an answer, the Lord's own reply -- 'write the vision... the just shall live by his faith' (2:4) -- and the five 'woe' oracles against the proud oppressor, closing on 'the Lord is in his holy temple: let all the earth keep silence before him.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Cross-chapter span (1:12-2:20) mechanically split into same-chapter range strings, canon-verified against data/compiled/canon.json before authoring.

label: A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth.
kjv_superscription: HAB.3.1, this closing prayer's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row) -- a second, distinct superscription within the same book, opening its own final unit exactly as Psalm 3's own does (Batch W3 precedent).
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. A psalm-like closing prayer, ending on its own musical notation ('To the chief singer on my stringed instruments,' 3:19) -- the same genre marker several Psalms carry.

label: The word of the Lord that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.
kjv_superscription: HOS.1.1, the book's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note. Content: the Lord's own command to take Gomer, a wife of whoredoms, and the three children named as living signs -- Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah ('not pitied'), Lo-ammi ('not my people') -- closing on the promise of restoration, 'ye are the sons of the living God.'

label: The estranged wife: judgment, then the valley of Achor for a door of hope
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Hosea 2, Israel pictured as an adulterous wife who forgot her true husband for her own lovers, the Lord's own judgment to strip and hedge her way, giving way to allurement and restoration -- 'I will give her... the valley of Achor for a door of hope' -- and a renewed betrothal 'in righteousness, and in judgment, and in lovingkindness.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: The second sign: buying back an adulteress for fifteen pieces of silver
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 3, a second commanded sign -- 'go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress' -- bought back for fifteen pieces of silver and barley, a living picture of Israel's own many days without king or sacrifice before their own eventual return to 'seek the Lord their God, and David their king.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: No truth, nor mercy, nor knowledge of God in the land
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 4, the Lord's own controversy with the land for its lack of truth and knowledge of God, priest and people alike corrupted, closing on Ephraim 'joined to idols: let him alone.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Judgment on priests and princes; Ephraim's own vain appeal to Assyria
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 5, judgment toward priests, people, and the house of the king, Ephraim's own appeal to 'king Jareb' of Assyria that could not heal them, and the Lord's own withdrawal 'till they acknowledge their offence, and seek my face.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Come, and let us return unto the Lord; Gilead's own city of iniquity
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 6, the call to return -- 'after two days will he revive us: in the third day he will raise us up' -- 'I desired mercy, and not sacrifice,' and the indictment of Gilead and the priests' own company of murderers.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Ephraim's own foreign alliances: they call to Egypt, they go to Assyria
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 7, conspiracies within the royal court pictured as an unwatched baker's oven, and Ephraim's own foolish courting of Egypt and Assyria -- 'a silly dove without heart.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: They have sown the wind, and shall reap the whirlwind: the calf of Samaria
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 8, kings and idols set up without the Lord, the calf of Samaria to be broken in pieces, and Israel's own covenant-breaking summed up: 'they have sown the wind, and they shall reap the whirlwind.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Rejoice not, O Israel: Gilgal's own wickedness, and a return to Egypt and Assyria
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 9, 'rejoice not, O Israel, for joy, as other people, for thou hast gone a whoring from thy God' -- exile pictured as a return to Egypt and unclean food in Assyria, and the days of Gibeah's own corruption recalled.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Israel is an empty vine: the multiplied altars broken down
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 10, Israel pictured as an empty vine whose increase only multiplied altars and idols, the calves of Beth-aven carried to Assyria, and the call to 'sow to yourselves in righteousness, reap in mercy.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 11, the Lord's own tender remembrance of Israel as a child led by cords of love, the Lord's own compassion overruling deserved judgment -- 'how shall I give thee up, Ephraim?... I am God, and not man' -- and the promise of a trembling return 'as a bird out of Egypt.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: Ephraim feedeth on wind: Jacob's own history recalled
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 12, Ephraim's own covenant-making with Assyria and Egypt rebuked, Jacob's own history recalled -- wrestling with the angel at Beth-el, serving for a wife in Syria -- and Ephraim's own deceitful balances.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: I will be unto them as a lion: yet I will ransom them from the power of the grave
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 13, molten images and calf-worship rebuked, the Lord's own judgment pictured as a lion, a leopard, a bereaved bear -- yet 'I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues' -- closing on Samaria's own coming desolation.
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: O Israel, return unto the Lord thy God; I will heal their backsliding
atlas_section: Hosea pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Hosea 14, the book's own closing call -- 'take with you words, and turn to the Lord... Asshur shall not save us' -- the Lord's own promise, 'I will heal their backsliding, I will love them freely,' and a final wisdom saying: 'the ways of the Lord are right, and the just shall walk in them.'
ref_note: GENERAL-kind, per this file's own header note.

label: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
kjv_superscription: ISA.1.1, the book's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: 'hear, O heavens, and give ear, O earth' -- the Lord's own indictment of a rebellious, sin-laden nation, and 'come now, and let us reason together' -- true repentance sought over empty sacrifice.

label: The faithful city become an harlot; Zion redeemed through judgment
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Isaiah 1:21-31, Jerusalem's own decline from a faithful city to a harlot's dwelling, judgment as the Lord's own purifying fire, and the promise: 'Zion shall be redeemed with judgment, and her converts with righteousness.'

label: The word that Isaiah the son of Amoz saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem.
kjv_superscription: ISA.2.1, a second, distinct superscription opening this book's own next major section, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).

label: The mountain of the Lord's house exalted; nations turn swords into plowshares

witnesses.ref_note: Isaiah 2:2-4 read directly against the compiled KJV text -- included here too, explicitly, so this event's own PARALLEL ACCOUNTS section is complete (the pw_bethany/72-row precedent: once any witness exists, the top-level book needs its own explicit row).

Micah 4:1-3 read directly against the compiled KJV text -- near-identical to Isaiah 2:2-4 in substance and much of its own wording ('the mountain of the house of the Lord... established in the top of the mountains... swords into plowshares... nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more' verbatim in both), but genuinely differs in places ('all nations shall flow unto it' ISA.2.2 vs 'people shall flow unto it' MIC.4.1; 'Come ye' ISA.2.3 vs 'Come, and' MIC.4.2) -- a second, distinct witness account, not a copy of the same container, per this project's own inerrancy doctrine (positive citation only, no manuscript-variance framing).

atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 2:2-4, the req 1b named parallel with Micah 4:1-3 -- 'in the last days... the mountain of the house of the Lord shall be established in the top of the mountains,' the nations streaming to it, and 'they shall beat their swords into plowshares, and their spears into pruninghooks: nation shall not lift up sword against nation, neither shall they learn war any more.'
ref_note: HOST of the req 1b Isaiah 2:2-4 || Micah 4:1-3 parallel -- see this file's own header note. Title is this project's own CC0 phrasing, not a literal kjv_superscription, since the two accounts' own wording genuinely differs in places ('all nations' ISA.2.2 vs 'people' MIC.4.1; 'Come ye' ISA.2.3 vs 'Come, and' MIC.4.2) -- the shared-title law requires a title TRUE AT EVERY ANCHOR, so a paraphrase honest to both, not a verbatim quote of either, is used.

label: The day of the Lord upon all pride: idols cast to the moles and to the bats
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 2:5-22, the Lord's own day against everything proud and lifted up, men casting their own idols of silver and gold 'to the moles and to the bats' and hiding in the rocks from his own terror.

label: Judgment on Jerusalem's own leaders; the haughty daughters of Zion
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 3:1-4:1, the Lord taking away Jerusalem's own stay and staff -- the mighty man, the judge, the prophet -- children and babes left to rule, and the haughty daughters of Zion, adorned in finery, stripped bare.

label: The branch of the Lord, beautiful and glorious
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 4:2-6, a remnant washed and purged, called holy, sheltered by the Lord's own cloud by day and flaming fire by night.

label: The song of the vineyard; six woes pronounced
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 5, the parable-song of the vineyard that brought forth wild grapes, and six woes against covetousness, drunkenness, mockery of God, calling evil good, self-conceit, and corrupt judges, closing on a nation raised up from far as the Lord's own instrument.

label: Maher-shalal-hash-baz; the overflowing river of Assyria
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 8, the sign-child Maher-shalal-hash-baz naming Assyria's own swift plunder of Damascus and Samaria, the river of Assyria overflowing into Judah 'even to the neck,' and the call to bind up the testimony and seek the Lord rather than familiar spirits.

label: Unto us a child is born: the government upon his shoulder
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 9, the people that walked in darkness seeing a great light, 'for unto us a child is born, unto us a son is given... and his name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace' (9:6), followed by the Lord's own outstretched hand still against a proud, unrepentant Ephraim and Israel.

label: Woe to Assyria, the rod of mine anger
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 10, woe to those who decree unrighteous decrees, Assyria named as the rod of the Lord's own anger yet itself proud and doomed for judgment, and a remnant of Jacob promised to return.

label: A rod out of the stem of Jesse; the wolf shall dwell with the lamb
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 11, a rod out of the stem of Jesse upon whom the spirit of the Lord shall rest, the peaceable kingdom where 'the wolf also shall dwell with the lamb,' and the Lord's own gathering of the outcasts of Israel from the four corners of the earth.

label: The song of praise: therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 12, a closing song of thanksgiving -- 'behold, God is my salvation... therefore with joy shall ye draw water out of the wells of salvation' -- closing the book's own first major section (1-12).

label: The burden of Babylon, which Isaiah the son of Amoz did see.
kjv_superscription: ISA.13.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: Babylon's own coming fall to the Medes (13:17), the day of the Lord as destruction from the Almighty, and a taunt-song against the king of Babylon crossing into chapter 14 -- 'how art thou fallen from heaven, O Lucifer, son of the morning!' (14:12) -- closing on Israel's own restoration and rest from sorrow.

label: The Lord's own purpose against Assyria
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 14:24-27, a short, separate oracle -- 'the Lord of hosts hath sworn, saying, Surely as I have thought, so shall it come to pass... that I will break the Assyrian in my land.'

label: The burden of Moab.
kjv_superscription: ISA.15.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: Moab's own cities laid waste, fleeing with weeping, crossing into chapter 16's own plea for refuge and a closing dated coda -- 'within three years, as the years of an hireling, and the glory of Moab shall be contemned' (16:14).

label: The burden of Damascus.
kjv_superscription: ISA.17.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: Damascus 'taken away from being a city,' Ephraim's own fortress likewise failing, and a closing woe against 'the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas' (17:12).

label: Woe to the land shadowing with wings, beyond the rivers of Ethiopia
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 18, a woe (not this section's usual 'burden' formula, a real formal distinction) against the land beyond the rivers of Ethiopia, its own swift ambassadors sent by sea, ending with a present brought to the Lord of hosts in Mount Zion.

label: The burden of Egypt.
kjv_superscription: ISA.19.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: Egypt's own idols moved, her waters failing, her wise counsellors become fools, closing on a remarkable reconciliation oracle -- 'in that day shall Israel be the third with Egypt and with Assyria, even a blessing in the midst of the land' (19:24).

label: Isaiah walks naked and barefoot three years as a sign against Egypt and Ethiopia
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 20, dated 'the year that Tartan came unto Ashdod... when Sargon the king of Assyria sent him' -- a real, historically situated sign-act (Sargon II's own Ashdod campaign is independently attested outside Scripture), but GENERAL-kind per this file's own header note: no reusable anchor for that campaign exists anywhere in this app's own compiled data.

label: The burden of the desert of the sea.
kjv_superscription: ISA.21.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: a grievous vision of Babylon's own fall -- 'Babylon is fallen, is fallen; and all the graven images of her gods he hath broken unto the ground' (21:9), the verse Revelation 14:8/18:2 later echoes (a translation/literary fact, not textual criticism).

label: The burden of Dumah.
kjv_superscription: ISA.21.11, this short burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: a two-verse watchman's oracle -- 'watchman, what of the night?... if ye will enquire, enquire ye: return, come.'

label: The burden upon Arabia.
kjv_superscription: ISA.21.13, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: the travelling companies of Dedanim, bread and water brought to the fleeing inhabitants of Tema, and Kedar's own glory to fail within a year.

label: The burden of the valley of vision.
kjv_superscription: ISA.22.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row) -- 'the valley of vision' is Jerusalem itself, this section's own real exception among the burdens against foreign nations.
ref_note: Content: Jerusalem's own false confidence in her defenses rebuked, closing on the oracle against Shebna the treasurer and the promotion of Eliakim, given 'the key of the house of David' (22:22) -- a verse Revelation 3:7 later echoes (translation/literary fact, not textual criticism).

label: The burden of Tyre.
kjv_superscription: ISA.23.1, this burden's own superscription, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: Tyre's own trading empire humbled after seventy years, closing this book's own burdens-against-the-nations section (13-23).

label: The earth emptied and made waste: the Lord shall reign in Mount Zion
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 24, opening this book's own so-called 'Isaiah Apocalypse' (24-27) -- the earth utterly emptied and spoiled for defiling itself under its own inhabitants, the city of confusion broken down, closing on the Lord of hosts reigning 'in mount Zion, and in Jerusalem, and before his ancients gloriously.'

label: A song of praise: he will swallow up death in victory
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 25, a song of praise for a strong city made a ruin, a feast of fat things prepared for all people on this mountain, and the promise -- 'he will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord God will wipe away tears from off all faces' (25:8), a verse 1 Corinthians 15:54 later echoes (translation/literary fact, not textual criticism).

label: A song of trust: thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 26, a song sung in the land of Judah -- 'thou wilt keep him in perfect peace, whose mind is stayed on thee: because he trusteth in thee' (26:3) -- and a promise of resurrection: 'thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise... awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust.'

label: Leviathan punished; Jacob's own root to blossom and bud
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 27, the Lord's own sore, great, and strong sword punishing leviathan the piercing serpent, the vineyard of red wine kept by the Lord himself, and the closing promise of Israel gathered 'one by one' from Assyria and Egypt to worship in Jerusalem.

label: Woe to the crown of pride, the drunkards of Ephraim; precept upon precept
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 28, opening this book's own second cycle of woes (28-33) -- woe to Ephraim's own fading-flower glory, the drunken priest and prophet who err in vision, the promise of 'a tried stone, a precious corner stone' laid in Zion (28:16), and the parable of the plowman, who does not plow forever.

label: Woe to Ariel, the city where David dwelt
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 29, woe to Ariel (Jerusalem), besieged yet delivered as in a dream, a people who honor the Lord with their lips while their heart is far from him, closing on the deaf hearing the words of a book and the eyes of the blind seeing out of obscurity and darkness.

label: Woe to the rebellious children that trust in Egypt; the way, walk ye in it
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 30, woe to children who take counsel not of the Lord and go down to Egypt for help, the promise of a teacher no longer hidden -- 'thine ears shall hear a word behind thee, saying, This is the way, walk ye in it' (30:21) -- and Assyria's own downfall by the voice of the Lord.

label: Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help, and trust in chariots
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 31, woe to those who trust horses and chariots rather than the Holy One of Israel -- 'the Egyptians are men, and not God; and their horses flesh, and not spirit' (31:3) -- and the promise that the Lord himself will defend Jerusalem.

label: A king shall reign in righteousness; until the spirit be poured upon us from on high
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 32, a righteous king and princes who rule in judgment, each as a hiding place from the wind, women at ease warned of coming desolation, until 'the spirit be poured upon us from on high, and the wilderness be a fruitful field' (32:15), closing on blessing for those who sow beside all waters.

label: Woe to the spoiler: the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 33, woe to the spoiler who himself shall be spoiled, the Lord exalted, closing this book's own second woe-cycle (28-33) on 'the Lord is our judge, the Lord is our lawgiver, the Lord is our king; he will save us' (33:22).

label: Judgment on the nations, Edom named; the line of confusion and the stones of emptiness
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 34, the Lord's own indignation upon all nations, Edom named at length as the day of the Lord's own vengeance for Zion's controversy, its own land turned into burning pitch, possessed by the cormorant and the bittern.

label: The desert shall blossom as the rose; the ransomed of the Lord shall return with songs
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 35, closing this book's own chapters 1-35 -- the wilderness glad and blossoming, the eyes of the blind opened and the ears of the deaf unstopped, a highway called The way of holiness, and 'the ransomed of the Lord shall return, and come to Zion with songs and everlasting joy upon their heads.'

label: Comfort ye, comfort ye my people, saith your God
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 40, opening this book's own third major section (40-66, the 'Book of Comfort') -- 'comfort ye, comfort ye my people... speak ye comfortably to Jerusalem,' the voice crying in the wilderness preparing the Lord's own way (40:3, the verse all four Gospels apply to John the Baptist -- translation/literary fact, not textual criticism), and the closing promise that 'they that wait upon the Lord shall renew their strength; they shall mount up with wings as eagles.'

label: The Lord of history challenges the idols to declare things to come
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 41, the Lord raising up one from the east (Cyrus, not yet named until 44:28/45:1), his own challenge to the idols -- 'shew the things that are to come hereafter, that we may know that ye are gods' -- and the repeated word to Israel: 'fear thou not; for I am with thee.'

label: Behold my servant: a light to the Gentiles
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 42, the first Servant Song (42:1-9) -- 'behold my servant, whom I uphold... he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles,' given 'for a light of the Gentiles' (42:6, Matthew 12:18-21 later cites this song directly, a translation/literary fact) -- followed by a new song of praise and Israel's own blind, deaf unfaithfulness rebuked.

label: Fear not: I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 43, 'when thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee... fear not: for I have redeemed thee, I have called thee by thy name; thou art mine,' the Lord's own witnesses called, and Israel's own transgressions blotted out 'for mine own sake.'

label: I am the first, and I am the last: Cyrus named as the Lord's shepherd
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 44, 'I am the first, and I am the last; and beside me there is no God,' a satire on the folly of idol-carving (44:9-20, a craftsman warming himself by half a tree and worshipping the other half), and Cyrus named outright as the one 'that saith of Cyrus, He is my shepherd, and shall perform all my pleasure... to the temple, Thy foundation shall be laid' (44:28).

label: Thus saith the Lord to his anointed, to Cyrus
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 45, Cyrus named again and called the Lord's own anointed (45:1), raised up though he 'hast not known me' (45:4-5), closing on 'every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear' (45:23, Romans 14:11/Philippians 2:10 later echo this, translation/literary fact).

label: Bel boweth down, Nebo stoopeth: their idols carried into captivity
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 46, Babylon's own idols Bel and Nebo pictured stooping, carried as a burden by weary beasts, set against the Lord who himself carries his people 'from the belly' and 'even to hoar hairs.'

label: Come down, and sit in the dust, O virgin daughter of Babylon
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 47, Babylon pictured as a proud virgin daughter brought down to sit in the dust, her own sorceries and enchantments unable to save her from the evil that shall come upon her 'suddenly.'

label: Israel refined in the furnace of affliction, yet not utterly cut off
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 48, Israel called obstinate from the womb yet refined (not as silver, 'but not with silver') in the furnace of affliction for the Lord's own name's sake, closing this book's own 40-48 section with the call: 'go ye forth of Babylon, flee ye from the Chaldeans.'

label: The servant's own mission: to restore Israel, and to be salvation unto the ends of the earth
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 49, the second Servant Song (49:1-13) -- 'the Lord hath called me from the womb... it is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob... I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth' (49:6) -- followed by Zion's own restoration and the promise that her own builders make haste while her destroyers depart.

label: The servant's own obedience: I gave my back to the smiters
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 50, the third Servant Song -- 'I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair: I hid not my face from shame and spitting' (50:6) -- the servant's own confidence that the Lord God will help him, and he shall not be confounded.

label: Awake, awake, put on strength, O arm of the Lord; awake, awake, put on thy strength, O Zion
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 51, a double call to awake -- first to the Lord's own arm, that once dried up the sea for Israel to pass over, then to Zion herself, to put on her own beautiful garments, for the uncircumcised and the unclean shall no more come into her.

label: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 52:1-12, Zion called to shake herself from the dust and put on her own beautiful garments, 'how beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of him that bringeth good tidings, that publisheth peace' (52:7, Romans 10:15 later echoes this, translation/literary fact), and the call to depart from Babylon, touching no unclean thing.

label: He was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 52:13-53:12, the fourth and climactic Servant Song -- a servant marred in visage more than any man, despised and rejected, 'he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities: the chastisement of our peace was upon him; and with his stripes we are healed' (53:5), 'he was numbered with the transgressors; and he bare the sin of many, and made intercession for the transgressors' (53:12).

label: Sing, O barren: the covenant of my peace shall not be removed
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 54, a call to the barren to sing, for her own seed shall inherit the nations, the Lord's own everlasting kindness likened to Noah's own flood-oath never to be repeated, and the promise: 'the covenant of my peace shall not be removed... no weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.'

label: Ho, every one that thirsteth, come ye to the waters
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 55, the free invitation to buy wine and milk 'without money and without price,' the Lord's own thoughts higher than our thoughts as the heavens are higher than the earth, and his own word that shall not return void, closing on the mountains and hills breaking forth into singing.

label: My house shall be called an house of prayer for all people
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 56, blessing on the stranger and the eunuch who keep the sabbath and hold fast the covenant -- 'even them will I bring to my holy mountain... for mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people' (56:7, Jesus quotes this at the temple cleansing, translation/literary fact) -- closing on a rebuke of Israel's own blind, greedy watchmen.

label: The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart; idolatry under every green tree rebuked
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 57, the righteous taken away from evil to come with no one noticing, idolatry under every green tree rebuked at length, and the closing word: 'there is no peace, saith my God, to the wicked' -- set against 'I dwell in the high and holy place, with him also that is of a contrite and humble spirit.'

label: Is not this the fast that I have chosen? To deal thy bread to the hungry
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 58, a fast of ritual without righteousness rebuked, the fast the Lord has chosen -- 'to loose the bands of wickedness... is it not to deal thy bread to the hungry' -- and the promise of light breaking forth and the Lord's own guidance continually, if the sabbath itself is honored.

label: Your iniquities have separated between you and your God; the Redeemer shall come to Zion
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 59, the Lord's own hand not shortened to save, but sin itself the separation between the people and their God, a long confession of violence and deceit, and the promise: 'the Redeemer shall come to Zion, and unto them that turn from transgression in Jacob' (59:20, Romans 11:26 later cites this, translation/literary fact).

label: Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 60, Zion's own coming light while darkness covers the earth, Gentiles and kings drawn to her own brightness, gates open continually, and the closing promise: 'the sun shall be no more thy light by day... but the Lord shall be unto thee an everlasting light.'

label: The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; to preach good tidings unto the meek
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 61, 'the Spirit of the Lord God is upon me; because the Lord hath anointed me to preach good tidings unto the meek... to proclaim liberty to the captives' (61:1-2, the passage Jesus reads and applies to himself at Nazareth, Luke 4:18-19 -- translation/literary fact, not textual criticism), closing on garments of praise for the spirit of heaviness.

label: Zion given a new name; watchmen set upon her walls, who shall never hold their peace
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 62, the Lord's own resolve not to rest until Zion's righteousness shines forth, a new name given her (no more Forsaken, but Hephzibah), and watchmen set on the walls who shall never hold their peace day nor night.

label: Who is this that cometh from Edom, with dyed garments from Bozrah?
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 63:1-6, a short, vivid oracle -- one mighty to save, his own garments stained as from a winepress, 'I have trodden the winepress alone... for the day of vengeance is in mine heart.'

label: A prayer recounting the Lord's own mercies: we are the clay, and thou our potter
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 63:7-64:12, a prayer recounting the Lord's own lovingkindnesses of old, 'doubtless thou art our father, though Abraham be ignorant of us' (63:16), and the closing plea -- 'we are the clay, and thou our potter; and we all are the work of thy hand' (64:8) -- over Zion's own present desolation.

label: I create new heavens and a new earth
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 65, the Lord sought by a nation that did not ask, a remnant preserved 'for my servants' sakes,' and the promise: 'behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind' (65:17), a child dying at a hundred years old, the wolf and the lamb feeding together.

label: The heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool: the Lord's own closing word
atlas_section: Isaiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Isaiah 66, the book's own closing chapter -- a contrite and humble spirit valued over ritual sacrifice, Zion bringing forth her children before her travail, joy for Jerusalem's own mourners, and a final, stark word of judgment alongside worship 'from one new moon to another' -- the whole book's own closing juxtaposition of comfort and warning held together to the last verse.

label: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin:
kjv_superscription: JER.1.1, the book's own opening superscription clause, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Date: 'in the thirteenth year of his [Josiah's] reign' (1:2), reused from the pre-existing theo-234. Content: the call -- 'before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee... I have made thee this day a defenced city' -- and the visions of the almond rod and the seething pot. Place: Anathoth (1:1) and Jerusalem (the call's own address, 1:15-18).

label: The Lord's own controversy with backsliding Israel: they have forsaken the fountain of living waters
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Jeremiah 2, Israel's own early devotion in the wilderness recalled against her present idolatry -- 'my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water' (2:13).

label: Return, thou backsliding Israel: circumcise yourselves to the Lord
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 3:1-4:4, the harlotry of Israel and Judah pictured at length, the call 'return, thou backsliding Israel... only acknowledge thine iniquity' (3:12-13), a new paragraph beginning at 3:6 continuing the same appeal, closing on 'circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart' (4:4).

label: Destruction from the north: the whole land shall be desolate
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 4:5-31, the trumpet blown for a nation coming from the north, Jeremiah's own anguish -- 'my bowels, my bowels! I am pained at my very heart' -- and the earth seen returned to formlessness and void.

label: Run ye to and fro through the streets of Jerusalem: is there a man that executeth judgment?
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 5, the search for even one just man in Jerusalem, the people's own refusal to fear the Lord who set the sand as a bound for the sea, and a horrible and filthy thing done in the land: the priests bearing rule by their own means.

label: O ye children of Benjamin, gather yourselves to flee: evil appeareth out of the north
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 6, the siege of Jerusalem foreseen in vivid military imagery, the people's own false cry of 'Peace, peace; when there is no peace,' and the Lord's own rejection of sacrifice offered without obedience.

label: Amend your ways and your doings: is this house become a den of robbers?
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 7:1-8:3, the temple sermon -- 'trust ye not in lying words, saying, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord, The temple of the Lord, are these' -- Shiloh recalled as a warning, the Lord's own refusal to hear Jeremiah's intercession, sacrifice to Molech in the valley of the son of Hinnom (Tophet) condemned, and the dead exhumed and scattered before sun, moon, and stars.

label: Is there no balm in Gilead? Oh that my head were waters, and mine eyes a fountain of tears
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 8:4-9:26, a people that refuse to return though even the stork and the swallow know their own appointed times, Jeremiah's own weeping over the slain of his people, and the closing word that boasting belongs only in understanding and knowing the Lord, not in wisdom, might, or riches (9:23-24).

label: Learn not the way of the heathen: the gods that have not made the heavens shall perish
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 10, the folly of a tree cut from the forest, decked with silver and gold yet unable to speak or walk, set against 'the portion of Jacob... the former of all things,' and Jeremiah's own closing prayer: 'O Lord, correct me, but with judgment; not in thine anger, lest thou bring me to nothing.'

label: Hear ye the words of this covenant: cursed be the man that obeyeth not
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 11:1-17, the covenant made with the fathers at the coming out of Egypt recalled and its own curse pronounced on those who have broken it -- Judah's own gods now as many as her cities, yet unable to save her in time of trouble.

label: The men of Anathoth plot against Jeremiah's own life; Jeremiah's own complaint
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 11:18-12:6, Jeremiah's own townsmen of Anathoth plotting to destroy him 'like a lamb or an ox that is brought to the slaughter,' and his own complaint -- 'wherefore doth the way of the wicked prosper?' -- met with the Lord's own hard answer: 'if thou hast run with the footmen, and they have wearied thee, then how canst thou contend with horses?'

label: The Lord's own lament: I have forsaken mine house, I have given the dearly beloved of my soul into the hand of her enemies
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 12:7-17, the Lord's own grief over his own forsaken heritage, many pastors who have destroyed his own vineyard, and a closing word of mercy even for the evil neighbor nations, if they will learn the ways of his own people.

label: The linen girdle marred and profitable for nothing; every bottle filled with wine
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 13, two sign-acts -- a linen girdle hidden by the Euphrates and found rotten, picturing Judah's own marred pride, and every bottle filled with wine, picturing a nation to be dashed one against another -- closing on Jerusalem's own shame uncovered and a plea for the queen mother.

label: The word of the Lord that came to Jeremiah concerning the dearth
kjv_superscription: JER.14.1, this section's own superscription clause, quoted verbatim (public domain KJV text, per LICENSES.md's own 'KJV text' row).
ref_note: Content: Judah mourning under a great drought, false prophets who prophesy peace and truth falsely rebuked, and Jeremiah's own intercession for a people the Lord will not spare.

label: Though Moses and Samuel stood before me, yet my mind could not be toward this people
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 15, the Lord's own refusal of intercession even from Moses and Samuel, Jeremiah's own complaint -- 'wilt thou be altogether unto me as a liar, and as waters that fail?' -- and the Lord's own answer: 'if thou take forth the precious from the vile, thou shalt be as my mouth... I am with thee to save thee.'

label: Thou shalt not take thee a wife, neither shalt thou have sons or daughters in this place
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 16, a sign-act by ABSENCE -- Jeremiah forbidden to marry or mourn or feast, a living sign of the desolation coming -- set against a closing promise that the Lord will yet bring his people again into their own land, and turn even the Gentiles from idols to the living God.

label: The heart is deceitful above all things: blessed is the man that trusteth in the Lord
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 17, 'the heart is deceitful above all things, and desperately wicked: who can know it?' set against the man who trusts in the Lord, likened to a tree planted by the waters, and a closing call to hallow the sabbath day.

label: Go down to the potter's house: cannot I do with you as this potter?
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 18, a sign-act at the potter's house -- the marred vessel remade as it seemed good to the potter -- the Lord's own right to build up or pluck up any nation according to its own turning, and a plot against Jeremiah's own life answered by his own imprecation against his persecutors.

label: Get a potter's earthen bottle... and break it, and say, Even so will I break this people
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 19, a second potter sign-act -- an earthen bottle taken to the valley of the son of Hinnom and broken before the elders and priests, 'even so will I break this people and this city, as one breaketh a potter's vessel, that cannot be made whole again.'

label: Pashur smites Jeremiah and puts him in the stocks; Jeremiah's own cry: cursed be the day wherein I was born
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 20, Pashur the priest, chief governor in the house of the Lord, striking Jeremiah and setting him in the stocks; Jeremiah's own renaming of him 'Magor-missabib' (terror on every side); and Jeremiah's own rawest lament in the whole book -- 'cursed be the day wherein I was born... wherefore came I forth out of the womb to see labour and sorrow?'

label: Behold, I will turn back the weapons of war that are in your hands
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 21, an oracle to king Zedekiah, who sent to inquire of Jeremiah as Nebuchadrezzar besieged the city -- the Lord himself fighting against Jerusalem, and the way of life set before the king's own house: execute judgment, or the house shall become a wilderness.

label: Go down to the house of the king of Judah: oracles against Shallum, Jehoiakim, and Coniah
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 22, a series of oracles against Judah's own kings by name -- Shallum (Jehoahaz), carried away never to return; Jehoiakim, who built his house by unrighteousness and shall be buried 'with the burial of an ass'; and Coniah (Jehoiachin), written childless as to the throne, for 'no man of his seed shall prosper, sitting upon the throne of David.'

label: Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep: I will raise unto David a righteous Branch
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 23, woe to the shepherds who scatter the flock, the promise of a righteous Branch who 'shall reign and prosper... and this is his name whereby he shall be called, THE LORD OUR RIGHTEOUSNESS' (23:5-6), and a long closing rebuke of false prophets who steal the Lord's own words from one another.

label: Make thee bonds and yokes: serve the king of Babylon, and live
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 27, a sign-act -- bonds and yokes made and sent to the surrounding kings and to Zedekiah himself -- the call to serve Babylon and live, and a warning against the prophets who falsely promise the temple's own vessels will soon return.

label: Hananiah breaks the yoke and prophesies falsely; his own death within the year
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 28, Hananiah the prophet breaking the wooden yoke from Jeremiah's own neck and prophesying Babylon's own defeat within two years, answered by Jeremiah's own iron yoke and the word that Hananiah himself would die that same year 'because thou hast taught rebellion against the Lord' -- and so it came to pass.

label: Build ye houses, and dwell in them: seek the peace of the city, for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 29, Jeremiah's own letter to the exiles already carried to Babylon -- settle, build, plant, marry, and seek the peace of the city, for the seventy years must run their course, closing on judgment against the false prophets Ahab, Zedekiah, and Shemaiah among the exiles.

label: Write thee all the words that I have spoken unto thee in a book: the days come that I will bring again the captivity
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 30, opening the 'Book of Consolation' (30-33) -- Jacob's own trouble likened to a woman in travail, yet 'they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king,' the incurable wound to be healed, and the Lord's own fierce anger not to return until his own purposes are fully performed.

label: A voice heard in Ramah: I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel
atlas_section: Jeremiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Jeremiah 31, 'a voice was heard in Ramah...
