atlas_section: Ezra pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezra 4, the adversaries' own offer to help rebuild rebuffed, their own hired counsel to frustrate the work throughout Cyrus's own reign, and a letter of accusation under Artaxerxes leading to a royal decree halting the work -- which ceased 'unto the second year of the reign of Darius king of Persia' (4:24).
ref_note: LITERARY-STRUCTURE FACT, disclosed per this file's own header note: verses 6-23 are a chronological digression -- the author illustrates that opposition recurred under LATER kings too (Ahasuerus, then Artaxerxes, both decades after the surrounding Darius-era narrative) before the narrative itself resumes Darius's own reign at verse 24. Dated across the broad span from the work's own initial hindering (Cyrus's reign) to its resumption under Darius (-520, matching ezr_temple_completed, immediately below).

label: Prophecies of Haggai
Prophecies of Zechariah
The temple is completed under Darius
atlas_section: Ezra pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezra 5-6, Haggai and Zechariah's own prophesying that restarts the work, Tatnai the governor's own inquiry and letter to Darius, the search of the royal archives that confirms Cyrus's own decree, Darius's own further decree for the work's support, the temple's own completion and dedication, and the Passover kept by the returned exiles.
ref_note: Dated from the prophets' own restarting of the work in Darius's second year (5:1, -520, per the pre-existing return narrative's own adjacent dating) through the temple's own completion, matching the pre-existing ret_jerusalem_temple (-516) exactly.

label: Consider your ways: the call to rebuild the Lord's house
atlas_section: Haggai pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Haggai 1, dated 'the second year of Darius the king,' the sixth month, the first day -- the Lord's own word by Haggai to Zerubbabel the governor and Joshua the high priest, rebuking the people's own cieled houses while the Lord's house lay waste, and their own obedience: 'they came and did work in the house of the Lord,' dated again to the twenty-fourth day of the same month (1:15).
ref_note: Date: 'the second year of Darius the king... the sixth month, the first day' (1:1), interpolated from the pre-existing theo-245. Place: Jerusalem, the temple site, implicit throughout via Zerubbabel/Joshua's own presence there.

label: The latter glory of this house shall be greater than the former
atlas_section: Haggai pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Haggai 2:1-9, dated the seventh month, the twenty-first day -- the Lord's own encouragement to Zerubbabel, Joshua, and the people to be strong and work, promising to shake the nations and fill the house with glory: 'the glory of this latter house shall be greater than of the former... and in this place will I give peace.'
ref_note: Date: 'the seventh month, in the one and twentieth day of the month' (2:1), same regnal year as hag_first_oracle_rebuild_the_house (2:18 confirms 'the second year of Darius' spans this whole book). Place: Jerusalem, unchanged.

label: The priests' own ruling on holiness and defilement; the Lord's blessing from this day forward
atlas_section: Haggai pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Haggai 2:10-19, dated the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month -- Haggai's own question put to the priests concerning holy flesh and defilement by a dead body, applied to the nation's own former unclean offerings, and the Lord's own promise: 'from this day will I bless you.'
ref_note: Date: 'the four and twentieth day of the ninth month... in the second year of Darius' (2:10), explicit. Place: Jerusalem, unchanged.

label: Zerubbabel made as a signet
atlas_section: Haggai pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Haggai 2:20-23, a second, distinct word 'the same day' addressed specifically to Zerubbabel -- the Lord's own promise to overthrow the kingdoms of the heathen and make Zerubbabel 'as a signet: for I have chosen thee.'
ref_note: Date: 'the same day' as hag_third_oracle_priests_ruling_on_holiness (2:20, 'and again the word of the Lord came... in the four and twentieth day of the month'), marked as a formally separate word by the text's own 'and again,' addressed to a different recipient (Zerubbabel alone, not the people generally) -- order_key=4 keeps it after its own same-day sibling in the global chronological timeline. Place: Jerusalem, unchanged.

label: Turn ye unto me, saith the Lord of hosts, and I will turn unto you
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Zechariah 1:1-6, dated the eighth month of the second year of Darius -- an opening call not to be as the fathers, who did not hearken to the former prophets.
ref_note: Date: 'the eighth month, in the second year of Darius' (1:1), interpolated from the pre-existing theo-246. Place: Jerusalem, implicit throughout via this book's own shared setting with Haggai.

label: The first vision: the horsemen among the myrtle trees
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 1:7-17, dated the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month (Sebat), second year of Darius -- riders patrol the earth and report it at rest, and the Lord answers with comfortable words: 'my house shall be built in it... and a line shall be stretched forth upon Jerusalem.'
ref_note: Date: 'upon the four and twentieth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Sebat, in the second year of Darius' (1:7), interpolated from theo-246. Place: Jerusalem, explicit throughout (1:12, 1:14, 1:16-17). First of eight night visions (the master brief's own named 'per vision' granularity).

label: The second vision: the four horns and the four carpenters
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 1:18-21, four horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem, and four carpenters (smiths) raised up to fray them.
ref_note: Same dated night as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Second of eight night visions.

label: The third vision: the man with the measuring line
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 2, a man measuring Jerusalem, told instead that the city shall be inhabited without walls, for the Lord himself 'will be unto her a wall of fire round about' -- closing on the call for Zion to escape Babylon while many nations join themselves to the Lord.
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Third of eight night visions.

label: The fourth vision: Joshua the high priest before Satan, and the promised BRANCH
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 3, Joshua the high priest standing in filthy garments before the angel of the Lord, with Satan resisting him; the Lord rebukes Satan, removes Joshua's own iniquity, and promises 'my servant the BRANCH,' a stone with seven eyes.
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Fourth of eight night visions.

label: The fifth vision: the golden candlestick and the two olive trees
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 4, an all-gold candlestick with seven lamps fed by two olive trees, and the word to Zerubbabel -- 'not by might, nor by power, but by my spirit, saith the Lord of hosts' -- his own hands having laid the temple's foundation shall also finish it.
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Fifth of eight night visions.

label: The sixth vision: the flying roll
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 5:1-4, a flying scroll twenty cubits by ten -- the curse that goes forth over the whole earth against thieves and false swearers.
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Sixth of eight night visions.

label: The seventh vision: the woman in the ephah
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 5:5-11, an ephah with a woman named Wickedness sealed inside it by a weight of lead, carried away by two winged women to be set up in the land of Shinar.
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Seventh of eight night visions.

label: The eighth vision: the four chariots
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 6:1-8, four chariots between two mountains of brass, the four spirits of the heavens sent to patrol the earth -- those toward the north country have quieted the Lord's own spirit there.
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_vision_1_horsemen_among_the_myrtles. Eighth and last of the night visions.

label: The crowning of Joshua the high priest: Behold the man whose name is The BRANCH
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 6:9-15, a real, narrated sign-act following the eight night visions -- silver and gold crowns made from the returned exiles' own gift and set upon Joshua the high priest's own head, with the promise, 'behold the man whose name is The BRANCH... he shall build the temple of the Lord... and he shall be a priest upon his throne.'
ref_note: Same dated setting as the night visions immediately preceding (no new date given, and 'the same day' framing continues from 6:10). Place: Jerusalem, the temple, explicit (6:12-15).

label: Should I weep in the fifth month? A question about the fasts
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 7, dated the fourth day of the ninth month (Chisleu), fourth year of Darius -- envoys from Beth-el ask the priests whether the mourning fasts of the exile should continue, answered first by a rebuke recalling the former prophets and the seventy years, and the call to execute true judgment and shew mercy.
ref_note: Date: 'the fourth year of king Darius... the fourth day of the ninth month, even in Chisleu' (7:1) -- a simple, text-explicit two-year forward count from the night visions' own 'second year of Darius' (theo-246's own -520 reused as the anchor), the same discipline 1samuel.toml's own 'twenty years after the ark's own capture' precedent already establishes. Place: Jerusalem, explicit ('the house of God,' 7:2-3).

label: The Lord's own answer: true judgment now, and joy and gladness to come
atlas_section: Zechariah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Zechariah 8, the Lord's own extended answer, formally distinct ('again the word of the Lord of hosts came to me') -- Jerusalem to be called 'a city of truth,' old men and women and playing children again filling her streets, the fasts turned to joy and gladness, and many nations coming to seek the Lord in Jerusalem, taking hold of the skirt of a Jew, saying, 'we will go with you: for we have heard that God is with you.'
ref_note: Same dated setting as zec_the_question_of_fasting (its own direct, formally-marked answer). Place: Jerusalem, explicit throughout.

label: The second temple completed in Jerusalem
Ahasuerus's feast; Vashti is deposed
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Esther 1, King Ahasuerus's own six-month display of his kingdom's wealth followed by a seven-day feast at Shushan the palace, Queen Vashti's own refusal to appear before the assembled princes, and the king's own decree deposing her on his counsellors' own advice.
ref_note: Dated to 'the third year of his reign' (1:3), the traditional identification of Ahasuerus with Xerxes I -- see this file's own header note.

label: Esther is made queen; Mordecai uncovers a plot
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 2, the gathering of virgins to the king's own house, Esther's own selection and coronation as queen in Vashti's own place, Mordecai's own instruction that she not reveal her own people, and Mordecai's own discovery of Bigthan and Teresh's own plot against the king's life, recorded in the chronicles.
ref_note: Dated to 'the seventh year of his reign' (2:16), when Esther was made queen.

label: Haman's plot to destroy the Jews
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 3, Haman's own advancement above all the princes, Mordecai's own refusal to bow to him, Haman's own furious plan to destroy all the Jews throughout the kingdom, the casting of Pur (the lot) to fix the day, and the king's own decree sealed and sent to every province.
ref_note: Dated to 'the twelfth year of king Ahasuerus' (3:7) -- see this file's own header note.

label: Mordecai's appeal; "for such a time as this"
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 4, Mordecai's own mourning in sackcloth and ashes at the king's gate, his own message to Esther urging her to intercede, his own warning that deliverance would arise from elsewhere if she stayed silent -- 'who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?' -- and Esther's own call for a three-day fast before she would go in unto the king unbidden.
ref_note: Same year as est_hamans_plot, immediately following it.

label: Esther's banquet invitation to the king and Haman
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 5, Esther's own appearance before the king unbidden and his own extension of the golden sceptre, her own invitation of the king and Haman to a banquet, a second banquet proposed for the following day, and Haman's own gallows built for Mordecai at his wife Zeresh's own suggestion, fifty cubits high.
ref_note: Same year, the third day after the fast (5:1).

label: The king honors Mordecai in the night
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 6, the king's own sleepless night and the reading of the chronicles that reveals Mordecai was never rewarded for uncovering the earlier plot, Haman's own unwitting counsel on how to honor 'the man whom the king delighteth to honour,' and his own humiliation leading Mordecai through the streets on the king's own horse.
ref_note: Same year, the night before the second banquet.

label: Haman's downfall at the second banquet
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 7, Esther's own accusation of Haman before the king at the second banquet, the king's own wrath, Haman's own fall upon Esther's own couch pleading for his life, and his own hanging on the very gallows he had built for Mordecai.
ref_note: Same year, the second banquet.

label: The king's new decree; the Jews may defend themselves
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 8, Haman's own house given to Esther and his own signet ring to Mordecai, Esther's own renewed plea before the king, and the new decree -- since the first could not be revoked -- granting the Jews the right to assemble and defend themselves throughout every province, met with light, gladness, and honour among the Jews.
ref_note: Same year, following Haman's own downfall.

label: The Jews defeat their enemies
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 9:1-19, the day appointed by Haman's own lot arrives, the Jews' own victory over those who hated them throughout the provinces and at Shushan, the ten sons of Haman slain, and Esther's own request for a second day at Shushan, establishing the days of Purim as feasting and gladness.
ref_note: Dated to 'the thirteenth day' of the twelfth month, Adar (9:1), within the same broad regnal year as the preceding crisis -- see this file's own header note.

label: The feast of Purim is instituted
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 9:20-32, Mordecai's own letters establishing the fourteenth and fifteenth days of Adar as an annual feast of gladness and gift-giving, named Purim after the lot Haman cast, and Queen Esther's own further letter confirming the observance in writing.
ref_note: Same year, the institution following directly from the victory just narrated.

label: The greatness of Mordecai
atlas_section: Esther pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Esther 10, a closing summary of King Ahasuerus's own greatness and tribute upon the land, and Mordecai's own advancement next to the king, 'great among the Jews, and accepted of the multitude of his brethren, seeking the wealth of his people.'
ref_note: A broad closing range, disclosed: the book's own final summary verses (recorded 'in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Media and Persia,' 10:2) span from the crisis just narrated to the traditional end of Ahasuerus/Xerxes I's own reign (-465), not a single dated moment.

label: Ezra's commission and arrival from Babylon
atlas_section: Ezra pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezra 7, Ezra's own priestly genealogy back to Aaron, his own skill in the law of Moses, King Artaxerxes' own letter granting him authority and provision, and Ezra's own blessing of the Lord for putting it in the king's heart.
ref_note: Traditionally dated to the seventh year of Artaxerxes I (7:7-8), circa -458 BC, a widely-used traditional identification -- disclosed as such, not independently re-derived.

label: Ezra's caravan journeys to Jerusalem
atlas_section: Ezra pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezra 8, the genealogy of those who went up with Ezra, his own search for Levites at the river Ahava, the proclaimed fast for a safe journey rather than asking the king for soldiers, the weighing out of the silver and gold entrusted to the priests, the journey itself, and the offerings and commissions delivered on arrival.
ref_note: Same year as ezr_ezra_arrives, the journey immediately following the commission.

label: Ezra's grief and prayer over the people's intermarriage
atlas_section: Ezra pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezra 9, the princes' own report that the people, priests, and Levites had intermarried with the surrounding peoples, Ezra's own astonished mourning and rending of his garments, and his own prayer of confession before the Lord at the evening sacrifice.
ref_note: Same year as Ezra's own arrival, shortly after it.

label: The assembly's confession; the list of those who had intermarried
atlas_section: Ezra pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Ezra 10, the great assembly weeping with Ezra, Shechaniah's own proposal of a covenant to put away the foreign wives, the proclamation gathering all Judah to Jerusalem within three days, the three-month inquiry by the heads of the fathers, and the closing roster of those found to have taken strange wives.
ref_note: Dated shortly after ezr_ezras_prayer, closing this book's own narrative.

label: Nehemiah hears of Jerusalem's ruin in Susa
Nehemiah hears of Jerusalem's ruin and prays
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0 -- no external PD source claimed): Nehemiah 1:2-11, Hanani's own report that Jerusalem's own wall lies broken down and its gates burned, Nehemiah's own days of weeping and fasting, and his own prayer of confession and petition before King Artaxerxes.
ref_note: Same year and place as the pre-existing ret_susa (-445, Susa).

label: Nehemiah completes Jerusalem's wall
Artaxerxes sends Nehemiah to Jerusalem
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 2:1-10, the king's own notice of Nehemiah's sad countenance in the month Nisan, Nehemiah's own request to be sent to rebuild the city of his fathers' sepulchres, the king's own letters granting timber and safe passage, and Sanballat and Tobiah's own displeasure on hearing of it.
ref_note: Dated to Nisan, 'the twentieth year of Artaxerxes' (2:1), leading directly into the pre-existing ret_jerusalem_wall (-444).

label: Nehemiah inspects the walls by night; announces the plan
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 2:12-20, Nehemiah's own secret night inspection of the broken walls and burned gates, and his own announcement to the rulers, priests, and nobles to rise up and build, met with Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem's own mockery.
ref_note: Dated to match the pre-existing ret_jerusalem_wall's own opening anchor (2:11, -444), the days immediately following Nehemiah's own arrival.

label: The roster of the wall's builders
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 3, the roster of priests, rulers, goldsmiths, merchants, and ordinary families who each repaired their own section of the wall, gate by gate, around the full circuit of Jerusalem.
ref_note: Dated to the wall-building's own construction period, the same year as neh_nehemiah_inspects_walls.

label: Opposition mounts; the builders arm themselves
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 4, Sanballat's own mockery and the conspiracy of the surrounding peoples to fight against Jerusalem, Judah's own weariness, and Nehemiah's own arrangement for half the builders to stand guard with weapons while the other half continued the work.
ref_note: Same construction-period year.

label: Nehemiah ends the oppression of the poor
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 5, the people's own great cry against their nobles for usury and debt-bondage during the famine, Nehemiah's own rebuke and the nobles' own agreement to restore what was taken, and Nehemiah's own account of his personal generosity as governor, never claiming the governor's own usual bread.
ref_note: Same construction-period year.

label: Further plots against Nehemiah; the wall is finished
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 6:1-14, 16-19, Sanballat and Geshem's own repeated attempts to lure Nehemiah away, Sanballat's own open letter of false accusation, the hired prophet Shemaiah's own attempt to frighten Nehemiah into sin, and -- after the wall's own completion -- the surrounding nations' own dismay at the work and Tobiah's own continuing intrigue by letter with the nobles of Judah, his own in-laws.
ref_note: Deliberately excludes only 6:15 itself (the wall's own completion date), the pre-existing ret_jerusalem_wall's own closing anchor (-444) -- verses 16-19 continue this same chapter's own narrative on the far side of that anchor and belong with the surrounding opposition narrative, not a separate container.

label: Gatekeepers, singers, and Levites appointed over the city
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 7:1-5, the appointment of porters, singers, and Levites once the wall and its doors stood finished, Nehemiah's own charge to Hanani and Hananiah over the city, the order to keep the gates shut until broad daylight, and Nehemiah's own decision -- with few people yet dwelling within the walls -- to gather the nobles and search out the genealogy of those who had first returned.
ref_note: req 1b NAMED CASE: the register Nehemiah found and re-published (7:6-73) is deliberately NOT a second top-level container here -- it is a real witness of Ezra 2 (data/curated/passages/ezra.toml's own ezr_list_of_returnees), not Nehemiah-unique content, so covering it again as its own container would collide anchors with that witness relationship (the same theo-162 lesson from this run's own 2chronicles.toml commit, applied proactively here rather than caught live by the validator). Witness row added in this same commit, immediately following this file in event-witnesses.toml.

label: Ezra reads the law; the feast of tabernacles kept
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 8, the people's own gathering as one man to hear Ezra read the book of the law from morning to midday, the Levites' own causing the people to understand it, the people's own weeping turned to a joyful feast day at Nehemiah's own word, and the feast of tabernacles kept with great gladness, 'such as since the days of Jeshua the son of Nun... had not the children of Israel done so.'
ref_note: Dated to the seventh month of the same year (8:2), following the wall's own completion.

label: A day of fasting; the Levites' prayer of confession
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 9, the children of Israel assembled with fasting, sackcloth, and earth upon them, separated from all strangers, confessing their own sins and their fathers' own sins, and the Levites' own long prayer recounting the Lord's own faithfulness from creation through the exile, closing in a sure covenant.
ref_note: Dated to the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month (9:1), the same year, shortly after the feast of tabernacles.

label: The covenant is sealed
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 10, the roster of those who sealed the covenant -- Nehemiah the Tirshatha, the priests, the Levites, and the chiefs of the people -- and the covenant's own specific commitments: no intermarriage with the surrounding peoples, sabbath and sabbatical-year observance, and provision for the temple's own service.
ref_note: Same year, the covenant following directly from neh_fasting_and_confession's own closing verse (9:38).

label: Those who settled in Jerusalem and the towns of Judah
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 11, the casting of lots to bring one in ten to dwell in the holy city, the roster of the chief inhabitants of Jerusalem by family, and the towns of Judah and Benjamin the rest of the people settled in.
ref_note: Dated to the same general resettlement period as the surrounding chapters.

label: Prophecies of Malachi
Nehemiah's second term: further reforms
atlas_section: Nehemiah pericope (this project's own sectioning, CC0): Nehemiah 13, the reading of the law that excludes Ammonites and Moabites, Nehemiah's own return from a period back at the Persian court to find Eliashib had given Tobiah a chamber in the temple courts, his own casting out of Tobiah's household goods, his own restoration of the Levites' own portions, his own enforcement of the sabbath against merchants trading on it, and his own confrontation of men who had married foreign wives, closing with his own repeated prayer, 'Remember me, O my God, for good.'
ref_note: Dated to 'the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes' (13:6), the text's own explicit regnal year, twelve years after Nehemiah's own first arrival (-445/-444) -- a straightforward arithmetic reading, not an independently-attested date.
